This creates a structural anti-predictive behavior at the top of the queue, where high-confidence predictions fail to materialize. The Brier score discrepancy (0.3617 vs 0.25) confirms overconfidence. The system's design enforces a two-tiered sorting approach: priced rows (from independent models) are prioritized over unpriced ones (based solely on confidence). The discriminator `rankingSource` enables this segregation without requiring changes to the engine or data schema. The failure mode arises when confidence alone dominates the ranking, leading to suboptimal task selection despite high confidence values. The empirical observation that confidence 91 yields the smallest positive edge while 85 yields the largest suggests a calibration issue in how confidence translates to actionable value.
